utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon, everyone. This is case number IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Prlic et al. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Registrar. I'd like to greet on this Thursday the 31st of May everyone here in the courtroom, the Prosecution, the Defence, the accused, and all of the people assisting us here. I'm going to given the floor to the registrar for a few IC numbers.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours. Several parties have submitted lists of documents to be tendered through Witness Rudy Gerritsen. The list submitted by 2D will be IC 588, while the list submitted by 3D shall be given the Exhibit number IC 589 under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Registrar. We'll now continue the cross-examination of the witness who testified in closed session. Therefore, we'll now move into closed session. Please draw down the blinds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's talk about the schedule for next week. As you know, we're going to have a hearing on Monday afternoon. It's a week where we should be sitting in the morning, but on Tuesday, the 5th of June, we won't be sitting in the morning but in the afternoon because of something related to a witness. Therefore, we'll be sitting in the afternoon on Tuesday and in the morning on Wednesday and Thursday. But I'm being told just now that there is no one on Monday. What's going on, Mr. Scott? You're always telling us you need a lot of time and there's no one on Monday.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: No, Your Honour there is not, and I'd indicated that to some -- to everyone and to some of the staff at various occasions. Because of various -- we indicated to the Chamber before, it's often very difficult to fit witnesses into four half-days in a week when you talk about people travelling long distances. When we schedule the witness who could only come on Tuesday afternoon, it was impossible to find a witness that would only fit into Monday afternoon. It's impossible to have a four-hour witness for cross-examination and redirect. It's never happened; couldn't do it. So, as I've informed everyone, including the counsel, and I believe including your staff, there is no witness on Monday. And the witness will start at 2.15 on Tuesday, and then we'll go back into morning sessions on Wednesday and Thursday. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just two minutes, if I may, for a brief submission. Yesterday, the Prosecution submitted a document entitled "Request to reply to the Defence responses to the Prosecution's motion for the admission into evidence of the transcripts of Slobodan Praljak's evidence in the case of Prosecutor versus Naletilic and Martinovic,". [In English] Your Honour, as a procedural point we note that despite the fact this request is entitled request to reply, it is plain from reading the submission that there is no request for relief of the Chamber to file the reply as required by Rule 126 bis. Instead, the submission is only a reply. Accordingly, this submission should be ignored as it does not conform to the rules and to all procedure and evidence of the Tribunal. I'm simply not in the position to write something on that because it is simply not foreseen by the rules, and that is why I'm just asking you to note that it -- that this document is not submitted as it should under the rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's not the case and the pleading speaks for itself and everyone can read it. It is titled, "A Request," and it's asked for request and it's in the first paragraph of the document to respond to points raised for the first time in the response by the Defence. It says so right on the front of the document. We think there are -- there are important points that the Chamber should consider, and we do ask in this instance to receive our reply. We don't always file replies and we know the Chamber's policy on that but it's very brief and it's directly responsive to issues -- arguments that the Defence have raised and we think the Chamber should have our reply. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Chamber will consider the issue. Mr. Kovacic, briefly, I see that you're raising the issue of the hard copy binders. I believe that you wanted us to work with the e-court system, but I absolutely disagree, because we need the documents. I can't use the e-court system whilst the witness is there answering a question, because if I have the binders, I can immediately consult the documents and control what is being said, and thus avoiding mistakes. I don't know what my fellow Judges think about it, but as far as I'm concerned we are going to continue using binders.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There must be some misunderstanding. I'm not raising that question at all, Your Honour. Just like all the other Defence teams, for each witness we prepared eight binders which were handed out as requested and agreed upon. However, the CLSS service last night sent an e-mail to all the Defence teams asking them to provide the binders for the interpretation service, which we do when we have time and means to do so and when we have documents to read out. Unfortunately, we can't do that all the time. We'd be very happy to do it, but we just haven't got the means. And so last night when I received this e-mail, I sent a lengthy reply because the interpretation service has asked us to increase this vast photocopying industry by 50 per cent, because if we have eight binders for the courtroom, and I agree with you they really are necessary for practical reasons otherwise we have to take e-court, which takes the amount of time it takes. Now we would have to provide four additional sets for interpretation. I agree that they would need it, but it's a problem which surpasses my means. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know that you're doing your utmost, but of course if one day you need the perfect translation of one document that is extremely important for you, please make sure that the translation department gets that document. I would like to thank you for all the efforts you do for the way you present these binders to us. It allows us to save time and work more efficiently. Just a few more minutes to deal with the following issue: We are conducting these proceedings at a regular pace. It's rarely happened for us to have to not sit, except for next Monday, but that's an exception. If we follow the same pace, we'll come to the end of the Prosecution case in a few months' time. Following that stage, you know that we reach the 98 bis stage, and possibly after the 98 bis stage we'll begin with the Defence case. And under the rules, in that case the Defence has to prepare its own list of witnesses and of exhibits. It's a great deal of work. There are six Defence teams here. It might be a good idea to consult each other, because it's probably not a good idea to have the same witness come here six times. You have to consult each other. You have to select your witnesses. And it's not something that you should do at the very last minute. I believe that you've already started. I'm not worried in any way, but I'd like to remind you of that fact because these lists will then have to be disclosed to the Judges, as the Prosecution did in their own time, in order for us to determine the amount of time you will be granted. Do not forget that point. For us it will be a great deal of responsibility to set the time that will be given to each of the teams and to the Defence as a whole, and we'll make that decision based on the lists of witnesses and exhibits. It's a great deal of work, so you shouldn't wait for the very last moment to think about this. It's something you should consider you now, because it's a great deal of work to identify your witnesses, your exhibits, et cetera. I'm perfectly aware of the amount of work you have to do in that respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me add something. [In English] More than the necessary translation. This does, of course, not mean that the Chamber has in any way taken any decision under 98 bis, and I'm aware of the fact that what the President suggests to you is in a way loaded with the risk of unnecessary work for preparation. I am not contradicting him, but I find it important to stress this. It is a situation that no one can change. We are all in a situation of insecurity. So in German there is an adage, which says, "To be ready is everything," and I thought it was important to bring this caution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I would like to add a French adage: "To govern is to foresee," and therefore a good Defence is to cover everything. So that's it. It is time to end these proceedings. Thank you very much. The hearing stands adjourned, and I will see you all on Tuesday afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 5th day of June, 2007, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 5.17 p.m.,
